chain.label: First officer's pattern of below-standard performance and minimal MD-10 landing currency
chain.trigger: She failed MD-11 proficiency checkrides in 1999 and 2001 and two DHC-8 checkrides in 1994, and had logged only about 25.6 hours and 2 landings in the MD-10 since February 2003.

chain.label: Machining tool marks in right main gear shock strut check valve hole
chain.trigger: Circumferential tool marks up to 0.0015 inch deep on the unthreaded surface of the check valve hole, with no preexisting fatigue.

chain.label: FedEx door/slide trainer differed from the airplane; no hands-on manual inflation handle training
chain.trigger: "there was no girt bar flap assembly (and, thus, no manual inflation or disengage handles) installed on FedEx's MD-11/-10 emergency exit door/slide trainer"

chain.label: Strong gusty northwesterly crosswind on runway 36R
chain.trigger: "MEM weather at 1225, wind from 320 degrees at 21 knots, with gusts to 26 knots"; the winds "would have required a pilot's constant attention, significant flight control inputs...and continuous modulation of those inputs."

chain.label: First officer neutralized crosswind alignment inputs below 100 feet; airplane drifted right in a left crab
chain.trigger: "as the airplane descended below 100 feet, the aileron and rudder control inputs were neutralized and remained neutral until the airplane touched down"

caused_by.evidence: "because there are no reasonable explanations for the first officer's failure to take corrective action during the late stages of the approach, and because of her history of poor performance"

"the winds at the time of the accident would have required a pilot's constant attention, significant flight control inputs along both the roll (control wheel) and yaw axes (rudder pedal), and continuous modulation of those inputs"

chain.label: First officer did not flare; descent rate never arrested before touchdown
chain.trigger: "the accident airplane's FDR data showed that the first officer did not increase the airplane's pitch attitude to arrest the airplane's rate of descent," although FedEx procedures require increasing back pressure at about 30 feet agl.

caused_by.evidence: "postaccident review of the first officer's training history and postaccident interviews suggested a pattern of below-standard performance"

chain.label: Captain/check airman failed to monitor the first officer and command corrective action
chain.trigger: "the captain, who was conducting a line check of the first officer, did not adequately monitor the first officer's performance during the final stages of the approach and landing at MEM and failed to take or initiate corrective action to prevent the accident"

caused_by.evidence: "as the airplane's drift to the right continued uncorrected, the drift became markedly notable from both pilots' seats as the airplane descended through about 60 feet"
"The captain had sufficient time to observe and react to the airplane's drift and the first officer's failure to arrest the airplane's rate of descent as it neared the runway."

chain.label: Neither pilot initiated a go-around from the deteriorating approach
chain.trigger: "Although the first officer had sufficient visual cues and time to recognize and correct for the deteriorating approach to landing...she did not do either"; investigators determined "it would have been possible to conduct a successful go-around if initiated at various points during the approach and landing."

caused_by.evidence: "The captain should have verbally prompted flight control actions, commanded a go-around, or taken control of the airplane for a go-around or landing."
"the airplane began to drift to the right and continued to drift to the right, with a 5 degree to 6 degree left crab angle, until it touched down"

chain.label: Hard, crabbed, off-centerline touchdown imposing loads beyond landing gear design
chain.trigger: "the airplane touched down extremely hard while still in a crab"; right main gear touched down at about 14.5 fps some 45 feet right of centerline, dissipating energy "about 34 percent greater than the design reserve energy requirement."

caused_by.evidence: "the first officer did not properly apply control wheel and rudder inputs to align the airplane with the runway centerline...as a result, the airplane touched down extremely hard while still in a crab"

"apply appropriate back pressure on the control column to arrest the airplane's rate of descent before touchdown" was not done; "the left main landing gear touched down at a rate of about 12.5 fps...and the right main landing gear touched down at a rate of about 14.4 fps"
"Investigators also determined that it would have been possible to conduct a successful go-around if initiated at various points during the approach and landing."

chain.label: Right main landing gear outer cylinder fractured in overstress and the gear collapsed
chain.trigger: "the excessive vertical and lateral forces on the right main landing gear during the landing exceeded those that the gear was designed to withstand and resulted in the fracture of the outer cylinder and the collapse of the right main landing gear"

caused_by.evidence: "the analyses revealed that peak lateral loads coincided with the excessive vertical loads"; fracture surfaces showed "rough features with chevron markings consistent with tensile overstress"

"The tool marks at the shock strut chamber check valve hole created a preferred site for initiation of the crack; however, the damage was too small to have caused the event if normal landing loads were involved."

chain.label: Fuel-fed fire developed on the right side of the airplane
chain.trigger: "After the gear collapsed, a fire developed on the right side of the airplane"; "A fuel-fed fire occurred after impact."

caused_by.evidence: "gouges in the runway from contact with the right engine began about 3,085 feet from the touchdown point"; the right wing and fuselage "exhibited substantial impact and fire damage"

chain.label: Airplane veered off the right side of runway 36R and came to rest in the grass
chain.trigger: "the airplane began to veer off the right side of the runway...About 1226:30, the airplane came to rest in the grass on the right side of the runway."

caused_by.evidence: "The right main landing gear collapsed after touchdown on runway 36R, and the airplane veered off the right side of the runway."

chain.label: Nonrevenue pilot mistakenly pulled both the manual inflation and slide/raft disengage handles at L1
chain.trigger: "the nonrevenue FedEx pilot who opened the L1 emergency exit mistakenly pulled both the manual inflation and slide/raft disengage handles because he was not sufficiently familiar with their location and operation"

caused_by.evidence: "FedEx's inadequate hands-on emergency procedures training and the differences between the trainer and the door/slide installation on the accident airplane contributed to the unintentional release of the slide/raft."

"As the postaccident fire developed on the right side of the airplane, one of the nonrevenue FedEx pilots opened the L1 emergency evacuation door and pulled the manual inflation handle on the evacuation slide/raft."

chain.label: L1 evacuation slide/raft separated from the doorsill, leaving no usable door exit
chain.trigger: "the slide/raft inflated, separated from the doorsill, and disappeared under the airplane"; the R1 exit was unusable because of fire and smoke.

caused_by.evidence: "thus separating the slide/raft from the L1 doorsill"

chain.label: Two occupants minorly injured evacuating on the cockpit window escape tapes
chain.trigger: "the first officer sustained friction burns to both hands while sliding down the evacuation tape" and the jumpseat occupant "sustained minor injuries when he landed on his right shoulder after he let go of the evacuation tape."

caused_by.evidence: "Because neither the L1 nor the R1 door could be used for the evacuation...the occupants evacuated through the captain and first officer sliding cockpit side windows and used the evacuation tapes."
"about 152 seconds passed between the time that the first and last occupant exited the burning airplane"
